Gemini-3.7-flash requests are answered as gemini-3.8-flash - Gemini API - Google AI Developers Forum

# Build with Google AI Forum 

Hi Everyone,

Starting June 19, 2026, the Gemini API will stop accepting requests from unrestricted API keys to prevent unauthorized usage and billing risks.

If your Google Cloud project has the Gemini API enabled and contains unrestricted keys, please restrict them immediately.

### What to do:

- Option 1 (Restrict existing keys): Go to Google Cloud Credentials, select your key, and under API restrictions, restrict it to Gemini API (generativelanguage.googleapis.com).
- Option 2 (New keys): Generate new restricted keys in Google AI Studio and update your code.

Note: Keys generated directly in AI Studio are restricted to the Gemini API by default.

# Gemini-3.7-flash requests are answered as gemini-3.8-flash 

## post by Joao_Silveira 4 days ago 

 Joao_Silveira 

Hi all,

We’re seeing that every generateContent request to models/gemini-3.7-flash comes back with “modelVersion”: “gemini-3.8-flash”. We tried different requests with different explicit thinking levels but the results are the same. It however does not happen for other models we tried (3.6 in example).

We reproduced it with:

`curl -sS "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-3.7-flash:generateContent" \
 -H "x-goog-api-key: $KEY" \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -X POST \
 -d '{"contents":[{"parts":[{"text":"Reply with OK."}]}]}' \
 | grep '"modelVersion"'
`

Expected modelVersion is `gemini-3.7-flash` but response was `gemini-3.8-flash`.

Can we tell if either 3.7 requests are indeed being served by 3.8 or if the model version field is reporting the wrong version?

 Me too (4) 

## post by Androz2091 1 day ago 

Hi, we received an email from Google saying all requests to 3.7 are routed automatically to 3.8.

## post by Mahesh_Sutar 13 hours ago 

Hello @Joao_Silveira ,

Yes, this is intended behavior. `gemini-3.7-flash` is deprecated as of October 8, 2026 (and removed from the Google AI Studio model selector), though the API endpoint is not shutting down and automatically routes all requests to `gemini-3.8-flash`. Please check out the Gemini deprecations page for more details.

results.text:
Google Retired Two Gemini Flash Models by Rerouting Them. Your Evals May Be Testing the Wrong Model · Harel Asaf

# Google Retired Two Gemini Flash Models by Rerouting Them. Your Evals May Be Testing the Wrong Model

On October 8, Google deprecated gemini-3.5-flash and gemini-3.7-flash and began routing requests to newer models. What the release notes say, why a working call is not proof of the same model, and a short checklist to detect and control the change.

By Harel Asaf· AI Builder· Tel Aviv

If your code calls `gemini-3.7-flash` or `gemini-3.5-flash`, it probably still works. That is the problem worth thinking about.

On October 8, Google deprecated both models and began routing their traffic to newer ones. The call succeeds. The model answering it is not the one you named.

An error would have been easier to deal with. A quiet substitution can pass every health check you have.

## What Google's release notes say

The Gemini API release notes for October 8, 2026 contain two relevant entries:

- `gemini-3.7-flash` is deprecated and replaced by `gemini-3.8-flash`. All requests to `gemini-3.7-flash` are automatically routed to `gemini-3.8-flash`.
- `gemini-3.5-flash` is deprecated and replaced by `gemini-3.6-flash`. All requests to `gemini-3.5-flash` are automatically routed to `gemini-3.6-flash`.

Both entries tell developers to update their model string, and no entry says calls will fail. The same release notes entry also deprecates a Deep Research agent, `deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025`, with a shutdown date of October 23, 2026. That one has a date and a named migration path.

The deprecations page lists both Flash models with "No shutdown date announced" and the routed replacement. It also says that listed shutdown dates are the earliest possible dates on which a model might be retired, and that Google will communicate exact dates with advance notice.

## Why a working call is not enough

For uptime, the routing does its job. Requests keep working.

For quality, it says less than you need. A different model can change verbosity, formatting habits, refusal boundaries, tool-calling behavior, and latency. Those changes do not raise an exception.

Think about what in a typical system would notice:

- Health checks see a 200 response.
- Error alerts see nothing.
- Pinned evals keep running, but if they call the old ID, their results now describe the replacement model, not the one the report names.
- Cost dashboards may move, in either direction.

This is a description of how the failure would look, not a report of any specific breakage. I have not tested the rerouted models against a production workload.

## What changed in price

Google's pricing page lists `gemini-3.8-flash` and `gemini-3.6-flash` at $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens through December 31, 2026, and $1.50 and $7.50 starting January 1, 2027, on the paid tier.

I could not find the deprecated models' earlier prices on Google's current pricing page, so I am not stating what a caller paid before. The independent analysis site Pick Right reports that the old 3.5 Flash rate was $1.50 and $9.00 and the old 3.7 Flash rate matched the new one. Treat that as a secondary claim.

The part I can state from Google's own page is the 2027 step. For the replacement models, every listed standard rate doubles on January 1, 2027. If you budget on these model families, use the 2027 numbers.

A simple hypothetical shows the size of it. A workload of 10 million input and 2 million output tokens per month costs $15.00 at the listed 2026 rates and $30.00 at the listed 2027 rates ($7.50 plus $7.50, then $15.00 plus $15.00). Your volumes will differ, and this ignores caching and batch discounts.

## A short checklist

None of this requires new tooling.

1. Find every pinned ID. Search code, config, notebooks, eval harnesses, and prompts-as-config for `gemini-3.5-flash` and `gemini-3.7-flash`.

2. Decide on purpose. Either move to the replacement ID

# Gemini API deprecates 3.7 Flash and silently routes it to 3.8 Flash; 3.5 Flash moves to 3.6, old Deep Research agent shuts down Oct 23

Bee Verified @thtbee_

Google's Gemini API release notes (Oct 8 entry) deprecate gemini-3.7-flash, with all requests now auto-routed to gemini-3.8-flash; gemini-3.5-flash is likewise routed to gemini-3.6-flash. The deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025 agent shuts down on Oct 23 and must migrate to the 04-2026 versions. Developers began receiving email notices on Oct 10.

## Key Takeaways

- ✓ Two model IDs silently re-routed: `gemini-3.7-flash` → `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash` → `gemini-3.6-flash`
- ✓ Same price: 3.8 Flash paid tier $0.75 in / $3.75 out per 1M tokens through 2026-12-31, then $1.50 / $7.50 from 2027-01-01
- ✓`deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025` shuts down 2026-10-23; migrate to `deep-research-preview-04-2026` or `deep-research-max-preview-04-2026`
- ✓ Deprecations page lists 3.6 Flash with no shutdown date, so 3.7 was replaced before its predecessor

Gemini Developer API pricing ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing

## In-Depth Technical Analysis

Google's Gemini API release notes (Oct 8, 2026) deprecate gemini-3.7-flash, which only went GA on Aug 13 and was succeeded by 3.8 Flash on Sep 2. Every request to gemini-3.7-flash is now automatically routed to gemini-3.8-flash, and gemini-3.5-flash is routed to gemini-3.6-flash. Developers started receiving email notices on Oct 10.

Because this is a server-side alias rather than a hard shutdown, calls keep succeeding, but the model actually answering has changed, so output style, token usage, reasoning length and tool-calling behavior may shift and eval baselines go stale. The deprecations page still lists 3.6 Flash with no shutdown date, so 3.7 was replaced ahead of its predecessor.

Pricing is unchanged: 3.8 Flash paid tier is $0.75 input / $3.75 output per 1M tokens through Dec 31, 2026, then $1.50 / $7.50. No new benchmarks were published with this change.

Also in the same entry: the deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025 agent shuts down on Oct 23, 2026; switch the agent parameter to deep-research-preview-04-2026 or deep-research-max-preview-04-2026. Action items: pin model strings explicitly, re-run your eval set, and migrate Deep Research before the 23rd.

# Gemini 3.7 Flash deprecation

By Steven Van · 2026-10-08

Requests now route to Gemini 3.8 Flash automatically, while an older Deep Research agent will shut down on October 23, 2026.

API requests to the deprecated gemini-3.7-flash model in Google Gemini are now automatically routed to gemini-3.8-flash. The announcement also covers migration from Gemini 3.5 Flash and an older Deep Research agent.

## Flash model migration

Developers using gemini-3.7-flash should update their model string to gemini-3.8-flash and review the Gemini 3.8 Flash guide.

Gemini 3.5 Flash is also deprecated, with requests to gemini-3.5-flash automatically routed to gemini-3.6-flash. Developers should change that model string to gemini-3.6-flash or gemini-3.8-flash and review the Gemini 3.6 Flash guide.

## Deep Research agent shutdown

The deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025 agent is deprecated and will shut down on October 23, 2026. Developers must update the agent parameter in their interactions.create requests to one of two newer versions:

- deep-research-preview-04-2026, designed for speed and efficiency and suited to streaming responses back to a client UI.
- deep-research-max-preview-04-2026, designed for maximum comprehensiveness in automated context gathering and synthesis.

results.author: Brett Gavaghan
results.text:
Gemini 3.7 Flash and 3.5 Flash deprecated in the API | Adaptd

# Google is swapping older Gemini Flash models for newer ones automatically, like a mechanic who upgrades your parts without ringing first

By Brett Gavaghan, Founder of Adaptd · 13 October 2026

On 8 October Google deprecated Gemini 3.7 Flash and 3.5 Flash in its API and started sending their requests to newer models. An older Deep Research agent shuts down on 23 October.

The short version

- Google deprecated Gemini 3.7 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash in the Gemini API on 8 October 2026.
- Calls to those models now go to Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.6 Flash automatically, and an older Deep Research agent shuts down on 23 October.
- If a tool your business uses was built on the Gemini API, ask the developer to test it on the newer model.

If someone built your business a quoting tool or an email sorter on Gemini, it may have had a brain transplant on 8 October. Nobody sent a card.

## What changed in the Gemini API?

Google's Gemini API changelog says Gemini 3.7 Flash is deprecated and replaced by Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Gemini 3.5 Flash is replaced by Gemini 3.6 Flash. Requests that still use the old model names are routed to the newer models automatically.

Google also deprecated its deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025 agent, which shuts down on 23 October 2026. Developers can move to a faster preview version or a 'max' version built for more thorough research.

## Who does this affect?

The change affects businesses whose tools or automations call the Gemini API directly, usually something a developer or agency built for them. The routing happens in the API, so nothing breaks overnight.

The catch is that a newer model can word things differently, lay out answers differently or follow your instructions a little differently, and the tool won't mention that anything changed. Technically correct, slightly unfamiliar.

## What should your business do about it?

Businesses with a Gemini-powered tool should ask whoever built it which model it calls, then test it on the newer one and update the model name.

My advice: keep a small set of real examples, such as ten enquiries and the replies you were happy with, and re-run them whenever the model changes. If anything relies on the old Deep Research agent, move it before 23 October or it simply stops. Automatic routing is better than an error message, but software, eh? Even the parts you never see get a service you didn't book.

Gemini API 3.7 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash: Current Running Models, Auto-Redirect Behavior, and Deep Research Pro Preview Migration - SmartScope

# Gemini API 3.7 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash: Current Running Models, Auto-Redirect Behavior, and Deep Research Pro Preview Migration

Key points of this article

All requests to gemini-3.7-flash are automatically redirected to gemini-3.8-flash, and all requests to gemini-3.5-flash are redirected to gemini-3.6-flash, while deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025 will shut down on October 23, 2026, requiring an update to its designation. Based on official documentation, this guide details the auto-redirection status and migration destinations for the agent parameter in interactions.create.

 3 min read · 569 words 2026-10-12 Published desk-research Method 

On this page

1. Legacy Flash Model Auto-Redirection and Current Behavior
2. Deep Research Pro Preview Shutdown Date and Agent Migration Targets
3. Model and Agent Migration Reference Table
4. Action Plan and Considerations Based on Usage Status
5. Sources

As of the verification baseline date of October 12, 2026, official specifications and migration procedures regarding model designations in the Gemini API were confirmed. For those operating with legacy model names set in their code, the primary questions are whether an immediate error will occur, which model is actually processing requests, and what code updates are required for preview features approaching their shutdown date. According to publicly available information, legacy Flash models are automatically redirected to successor models, but the Deep Research agent scheduled for shutdown requires explicit parameter updates.

## Legacy Flash Model Auto-Redirection and Current Behavior

All requests to gemini-3.7-flash are automatically redirected to and processed by gemini-3.8-flash (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog). In the official documentation for the specific model as well, gemini-3.7-flash is marked as deprecated, and it can be confirmed from the displayed content on screen that all requests are automatically redirected to gemini-3.8-flash (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.7-flash).

Similarly, all requests to gemini-3.5-flash are automatically redirected to gemini-3.6-flash (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog). Therefore, calling the API using legacy Flash model names does not result in an immediate cutoff error. However, the specific impacts of auto-redirection on quality, pricing, and latency have not been tested via actual measurements on production environments at this time and remain unverified.

## Deep Research Pro Preview Shutdown Date and Agent Migration Targets

Unlike legacy Flash models, the legacy Deep Research preview has a defined end-of-service date. According to the official changelog, deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025 is scheduled to shut down on October 23, 2026 (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog).

To continue using the feature, the agent parameter must be updated in interactions.create calls (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog). The two officially announced migration destinations are as follows:

- deep-research-preview-04-2026
- deep-research-max-preview-04-2026

Before reaching the shutdown date on October 23, preparations must be made to switch the agent parameter in caller code to one of the above identifiers.

## Model and Agent Migration Reference Table

The current operational status of legacy models and the legacy agent, along with response policies, are summarized in the following table.

| Legacy Identifier | Type | Official Behavior / Policy | Migration Target Identifier | Deadline / Announcement Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gemini-3.7-flash | API model | Deprecated, all requests automatically redirected | gemini-3.8-flash | Announced on October 8, 2026 |
| gemini-3.5-flash | API model | All requests automatically redirected | gemini-3.6-flash | Announced on O
